title: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
mutable_substrate: A shared multi-agent workspace at every archive node: meta-agent code, task agents, learned evaluators, shared infrastructure, prompts, and role-specific modules; the scoring/orchestration harness is fixed.
optimization_operator: HGM-style archive tree search expands a selected node through meta-agent code edits; Thompson sampling uses clade metaproductivity, with role/task load balancing and checkpointed evaluator replacement.
feedback_selection: Evaluator-independent roles use fixed validation benchmarks; evaluator-dependent roles use an epoch-frozen learned judge. Challengers replace incumbents only through epsilon-best-belief on a held-out ground-truth anchor, followed by selective erasure of displaced-judge records.
archive_memory: A tree archive preserves node topology, code, training evidence, anchor evidence, cached artifacts, and unrelated-role outcomes. Evaluator-dependent utility records are epoch-local and erased on slot replacement; cached artifacts can be rejudged lazily.
validation_strategy: Training feedback creates nodes, disjoint validation evidence drives search, and held-out tests or fixed post-hoc reviewer/grader panels report endpoints. Writer and prover candidates are only epoch-local winners because their search utilities change.
adaptation_mode: Offline co-evolutionary archive search with piecewise-stationary evaluator epochs; not runtime adaptation.
benchmarks: paper writing scored by four fixed reviewers
proof writing scored by three fixed graders
principal_results: Polyglot specialist and generalist each pass 119/166 held-out tasks (71.7%) versus HGM-HyperAgents 116/166 (69.9%), at 1.35x-1.72x lower search-token cost.
The matched-cost writer reaches 38.8% panel acceptance versus 21.8% for HGM-HyperAgents (1.78x); the best specialist reaches 40.5% (1.86x).
The specialist prover scores 4.33/7 and 61.7% Pass@6 versus static 4.07 and 55.0%, but its 48.3% Pass@7 trails the static prover's 55.0%.
The co-evolved grader improves ground-truth accuracy by 9% and reaches its specialist point at 3x lower search cost than HGM-HyperAgents.
The adversarial reviewer retains 80% anchor accuracy while accepting human and AI papers at similar rates; the strongest baseline over-accepts AI papers by up to 1.91x.
No-erasure archive rankings remain highly correlated with the displaced evaluator (Spearman rho at least 0.90), while selective erasure produces durable re-ranking.
Nemotron task-agent calls approach the GPT-only paper endpoint at an estimated 13x lower price-equivalent search-token cost.
limitations: Guarantees hold only within fixed-evaluator epochs and do not establish global agent-evaluator convergence, transition bounds, or erased-evidence regret.
Anchor quality bounds evaluator quality; APRES and IMO-GradBench labels may be weak or biased.
No human grading of generated papers or proofs is reported.
Short horizons, three domains, one foundation model for headline runs, and no unified cross-domain tree limit generality.
Task-agent best-belief values are incomparable across evaluator epochs and must be scored post-hoc.
Inherited tree topology may reflect expansion decisions made for obsolete evaluators.
Mechanism ablations use Nemotron rather than the GPT-5.1 headline setting.
The hand-crafted scheduler, replacement gate, and immutable harness remain outside self-improvement.
safety_controls: Replacement uses a fixed held-out ground-truth anchor and conservative epsilon-best-belief lower bound.
Ties retain the incumbent to avoid unnecessary transitions.
Selective erasure prevents stale scores from different evaluators being mixed.
Training, validation, and test evidence are separated.
The orchestration and scoring harness is fixed.
These controls do not prevent weak-anchor drift, generator-evaluator collusion, objective misspecification, or long-horizon cycling.

explicit_predecessors.name: Darwin Gödel Machine
explicit_predecessors.evidence: RQGM inherits archive search over self-modifying agents and contrasts DGM's node utility with later clade-level selection.

explicit_predecessors.name: Huxley Gödel Machine
explicit_predecessors.evidence: RQGM uses HGM clade metaproductivity, Thompson sampling, epsilon-best-belief selection, and its within-epoch guarantees.

explicit_predecessors.name: HyperAgents
explicit_predecessors.evidence: RQGM extends HyperAgents' meta-agent/task-agent nodes into shared multi-role workspaces containing co-evolving evaluator roles.

explicit_predecessors.name: Gödel Machine
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The paper frames empirical archive search as an approximation to proof-based beneficial self-modification.

explicit_predecessors.name: LLM-as-a-judge systems
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Learned reviewers and graders build on model judges, while controlled evolution targets their known biases.

explicit_predecessors.name: Self-play and classical co-evolution
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The Red Queen framing adapts moving-target competition from self-play and evolutionary computation to learned utility functions.

open_questions: Can global convergence or bounded regret be established across evaluator transitions?
How can evaluator progress be audited independently of a weak or biased anchor?
Will long-horizon co-evolution compound improvement, cycle, or collapse through collusion?
How sensitive are results to epsilon, checkpoint spacing, anchor size, and erasure policy under the headline model?
Can off-policy rejudging provide a common scale across evaluator epochs?
What immutable safety constraints should govern objective changes and adversarial pools?
Does the curriculum effect generalize beyond coding and intellectual artifacts?
When is changing the objective normatively justified rather than merely improving the evaluator?
